findings.fix: Name the involution explicitly, e.g. `have hsq : ((-1 : K) ^ (q.natDegree - j)) ^ 2 = 1 := by rw [← pow_mul, mul_comm, pow_mul]; simp`, then close with `linear_combination`/`ring` against `hsq` instead of `ring_nf; simp`.

The remaining content is only that `((-1) ^ (q.natDegree - j)) ^ 2 = 1`, but the final `simp` is tuned to whatever shape `ring_nf` produces (note the hand-supplied `mul_comm _ 2` fixing an argument order that `ring_nf` chose); any change to `ring_nf`'s normal form breaks it.

findings.evidence: Polynomial.lean:99-116 vs Basic.lean:159-173 — both run `by_cases h₁ : (l : ℕ) ≤ d`, then `by_cases` on `d ≤ l.val + n`/`+ m`, then `coeff_eq_zero_of_natDegree_lt (by omega)`, around `coeff_X_pow_mul'`.

findings.evidence: Euclidean.lean:69-72: `hbound` bounds `(X ^ l.val * a).natDegree ≤ l.val + a.natDegree` and `ha : a.natDegree + n ≤ m`; the goal `… < m - j` needs `l.val < n - j`, which comes from `l : Fin (n - j)`, not from `hj`. Mathematically, for `j > n` every column is a `castAdd` column reading `q.coeff` only, so the statement is independent of the left input.
findings.fix: Drop `hj` from `subresultantCoeffMatrix_add_mul`, `subresultantCoeff_add_mul_left` (line 86), `psc_add_mul_left` (line 94) and `subresultant_add_mul_left` (line 102), and correspondingly stop requiring `hj : j ≤ q.natDegree` in `subresultantCoeff_mod_left`/`psc_mod_left`/`subresultant_mod_left` (lines 115, 134, 141), which only forward it.
findings.issue: `hj : j ≤ n` is a redundant hypothesis. It is not needed by any step: the only place it could be used is the `omega` at line 72, which already relies on `l.isLt : l.val < n - j` (otherwise `l.val` is unbounded and the omega could not close), and that bound alone discharges both `j ≤ n` and `j > n` (then `n - j = 0` and the branch is vacuous). It is then propagated unnecessarily into the public API.

findings.evidence: Euclidean.lean:73-78; `Polynomial.toFn` is `LinearMap.pi fun i ↦ lcoeff R i` (mathlib/Mathlib/Algebra/Polynomial/OfFn.lean:34) with no entrywise apply lemma; TauCeti/Algebra/Polynomial/OfFn.lean already hosts the `ofFn`/`toFn` supplements.
findings.fix: Put both in `TauCeti/Algebra/Polynomial/OfFn.lean`, which exists for exactly this: a `Polynomial.toFn_apply : toFn n p i = p.coeff i` simp lemma (so `hpoly` needs no `LinearMap.pi` unfolding) and `Polynomial.ofFn_single : ofFn n (fun i => if i = l then 1 else 0) = X ^ l.val`.
findings.issue: Two reusable `ofFn`/`toFn` facts are buried as inline `have`s and proved by unfolding internals: `hpoly` via `simpa [toFn, LinearMap.pi]` (unfolds the `LinearMap.pi` structure because no `toFn_apply` lemma exists), and `hright`, which is the general fact `ofFn n (Pi.single l 1) = X ^ l.val`, unrelated to subresultants.

summary: The reduction argument is structurally sound, but the key entry computation closes by unfolding `reductionShear`, `Matrix.mulVec` and `dotProduct` inside one opaque `simpa`, the signed-remainder lemma ends in `ring_nf` plus a simp set tuned to its output, and a ten-line case-analysis block is duplicated for the third and fourth time instead of being factored out.
